paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: The effect of context masking perturbations by tag. Error bars indicate the standard deviation.
model_annotation: The chart illustrates the measured “effect” of context masking perturbations across four morphosyntactic tags, with six model/setting conditions shown for each tag and vertical error bars indicating standard deviation. The horizontal axis is labeled “tag” and lists the categories case, gender, number, and tense in that left-to-right order; within each category the bars are arranged as a grouped set of six. The vertical axis is labeled “effect” and uses a linear numeric scale with tick marks shown at regular intervals (0, 5, 10, 15, 20), spanning from slightly below 0 to a little above 20. A legend at the upper right maps colors to conditions: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (pink), and XLM-B₂ (red). For the case tag, the bars are approximately 6.0 (mBERT-L₂), 5.5 (XLM-L₂), 2.8 (mBERT-R₂), 2.1 (XLM-R₂), 12.3 (mBERT-B₂), and 11.2 (XLM-B₂), with comparatively large error bars (several extending from near 0 up into the low teens or higher). For gender, the grouped bars are about 1.4 (mBERT-L₂), 0.3 (XLM-L₂), 1.8 (mBERT-R₂), 1.0 (XLM-R₂), 4.2 (mBERT-B₂), and 3.4 (XLM-B₂), again with visible standard-deviation whiskers. For number, the bars are roughly 1.2 (mBERT-L₂), 0.8 (XLM-L₂), 1.0 (mBERT-R₂), 0.6 (XLM-R₂), 2.8 (mBERT-B₂), and 2.4 (XLM-B₂), with error bars extending above and below each mean. For tense, the bars are clustered near zero at about 0.4 (mBERT-L₂), slightly below or near 0 (XLM-L₂), slightly below or near 0 (mBERT-R₂), slightly below or near 0 (XLM-R₂), 0.5 (mBERT-B₂), and 0.6 (XLM-B₂), with smaller absolute bar heights but still noticeable uncertainty bars. The categories are not sorted by value; they appear in the fixed tag order, and no individual bar is visually emphasized beyond the consistent color coding and the presence of error bars.
